excerpt: Use our native integration, or manually connect with our hosted MCP url. Each agent gets its own identity on monday.
Connect agents from Claude, ChatGPT, Make, or any provider through a managed connection or a simple webhook — or build code-first with the apps framework.
Create custom board views, item views, dashboard widgets, and full-page apps.
Build with Vibe, monday's open-source React components, and look native instantly.
Deploy to isolated sandboxes monday manages. Your syncs and tools run on our infra, not yours.
Request granular scopes like `boards:read`. Store keys in managed secret storage.
Subscribe to `create_item`, `change_column_value`, and more.
Wire your apps and agents to leading providers — Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI — through one unified Models API.
Run and manage every monday agent programmatically from your own code, anywhere you need it.
Scope each agent's board access from the admin, audit every action it takes, and track AI credit spend across the whole org — all from one dashboard.
Talk to agents like teammates. Message them in updates, assign them items, and @mention them in any conversation to kick off real work — replies, statuses, and follow-ups included.
Bring an agent in once and reach it from Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram, Make, our MCP, or the API. One identity, every surface — no rebuilding per channel.
Build agents for your exact needs. Define the goal, set the rules, watch the results.
Describe any workflow in your own words to create a unique agent in minutes.
I tried using Monday.com for a building project I had and the interface became totally unusably slow... no idea if this is fixed but it seems like an issue for a billion dollar company.
Monday is just plain bad, it's slow, it's not really useful. Looks like a bunch of solutions looking for problems put together in a frenzy.
Moving from Trello to monday.com was the biggest reason why we couldn't deliver an iOS project on time. The team hated it, updating tickets once a week instead of daily. We're back on Trello now.

I use it at my current company. I don't like it. Jira is still far superior. Linking tickets to one another in Monday is really bad, data gets lost all the time, it's not good for retaining a record of work.
I worked at a company where Monday was the main interface between the back-office and the B2B clients we serviced. That was about as bad as you can expect.

This is one of the worst tools I've ever used and we tried hard for a year. The interface is clunky and slow and lets you delete important things on accident with multiple people having fallen victim to its non-intuitive UI.
We'd tried it for a little bit for a small 5-6 person team. It was slow as hell. Stopped using it.
Monday.com always seemed to re-label known practices with their own terminology. What am I missing? A ton of similar tools are already popular: Asana, all the ones from Atlassian.
Not related to the IPO, but has anyone else found Monday.com's branding to be very similar to Slack's? Specifically the logo palette, shape, and typeface.

Honestly, the end result was a lot worse than I expected. Using Redis & Cassandra as 1 db when your requirements were unlimited tables, fast filter/sort, etc. Literally the worst of all worlds imaginable.
Article shows that Cassandra is slow to retrieve data, so they added Redis as a cache to fetch recent events from there.

From ~8 seconds to ~3 seconds to fetch 5,000 items seems like going from horrible to still really actually pretty bad. Just about any SQL server with well defined schema and indexes would blow this out of the water.
A client of mine forced us onto Monday, and the un-opinionated style made it quite crappy. You can basically do whatever all managers came up with randomly and it sucked.
I'm amazed that a non-database company thought it was a good idea to write their own database in 2023, and astounded when they admit it publicly.

I used monday.com a few years ago when it was called 'dapulse'. I really wanted to like it because of how clean it was, but it required too much setup and customization for my liking. My team ended up switching back to GitHub issues/projects/milestones.
I used it a few times, it's as good as the others. I don't think there will ever be a silver bullet - the real issues are people issues.
If AI could 10x engineers, companies would be keeping people and making more money. This is just layoffs blamed on AI. (Reaction to Monday.com laying off hundreds to focus on AI.)
